Accessed Jul. 14, 2026. Back to top

title: Dark mode is now live in the Lugg app
summary: Dark mode is live across the Lugg app and web. You pick: On, Off, or let your settings decide — and yes, the live map goes dark too.
body_text: Dark mode is here. As of this week, you can switch Lugg to a darker, low-light look across the board — the iOS app, the Android app, and the web at app.lugg.com. Open Lugg, go to Settings , and pick On , Off , or System settings . That's the whole thing. If you've ever opened Lugg in a dark room and immediately regretted it, this one's for you. It's been one of the most-requested changes — and booking movers at 11 p.m. shouldn't feel like getting flashbanged by your own phone. Now it doesn't. What's new The details Feature Dark mode for the Lugg app Where iOS app, Android app, and web at app.lugg.com How to find it Settings → Dark mode Your options On, Off, or System settings (matches your device) Cost Free — it's just there How to turn on dark mode in the Lugg app It takes about ten seconds, and it works the same on iOS, Android, and the web. 1: Open Settings Tap your profile, then open Settings (the gear). On the web, you'll find it in the same menu at app.lugg.com. 2: Find Dark mode It's the first option at the top of the Settings screen. 3: Pick your look Choose On for dark all the time, Off for the classic light look, or System settings to let your phone decide — light during the day, dark at night, automatically. That's it. The change is instant, and it sticks until you change it again. Don't see the option yet? Update to the latest version of the Lugg app, or refresh app.lugg.com on the web. Light, dark, or let your phone decide The real point here is control, you decide how dark mode works. Keep Lugg dark around the clock, stay on the classic light look, or let your phone flip it for you on its own schedule. No single look gets forced on you. That control matters more than it sounds. When X removed its in-app dark mode toggle in March 2026 — forcing everyone onto their device's setting — users pushed back. Not because dark mode disappeared, but because the choice did. You're the one who knows whether you're booking a move at noon or midnight, so you should be the one who picks. So is dark mode actually better for you? It depends on you — your eyes, your screen, and the time of day. Here's the honest breakdown, not the hype, so you can pick what fits. For late-night use, dark mode is genuinely easier on the eyes in a dim room — less bright light blasting at you when you're checking your move at midnight. That's the number-one reason people ask for it, and it's a fair one. A Purdue University study found dark mode saves about 3–9% of battery at typical indoor brightness on OLED and AMOLED screens — and close to nothing on older LCD phones, where the screen lights every pixel either way. Helpful at 2% battery on moving day. Nielsen Norman Group research notes that light mode is generally easier to read for people with normal vision — and the advantage grows as the text gets smaller. So dark mode isn't a clear upgrade for everyone. It's better for some people, in some moments — which is exactly why it stays your call, not ours. One nice touch, whichever you choose: when dark mode is on, the live-tracking map goes dark too. Watching your Lugg movers head to pickup at night now looks the way a map app should after dark. Set it once, forget it Dark mode is the kind of small thing that makes an app feel like it was built for actual humans who use their phones at night. Head to Settings, pick the look you want, and get back to the part that matters — booking same-day movers and a truck in a few taps, with upfront pricing, real-time tracking, and no hourly minimums. Now in whatever shade you like.

title: Entergy Mississippi prepared for storms as the height of 2026 hurricane season approaches
summary: A below-normal hurricane season expected, but Entergy Mississippi customers urged to stay prepared
body_text: JACKSON, Miss. – As the height of the hurricane season approaches, Entergy Mississippi is prepared for summer storms, including hurricanes, and encourages customers to prepare as well. Scientists anticipate the 2026 hurricane season will have somewhat below-normal activity, with nine named storms expected, including four hurricanes – one of which could become a major hurricane. Regardless of how the season unfolds, we are ready — and we want customers to be ready, too. “As we enter the peak of hurricane season, our focus remains on delivering safe, reliable and affordable energy to the communities we serve,” said Kamisha Quates, vice president, reliability. “Our teams work year-round to strengthen our systems, train our crews and enhance our emergency response plans so we can restore power quickly and safely after storms impact our communities.” To enhance the reliability of our energy grid, Entergy continues to invest in infrastructure improvements, including upgrading existing systems, implementing vegetation management, and deploying smart grid technologies. These efforts aim to minimize storm-related outages and ensure reliable service, while keeping customer costs as low as possible. “Reliability remains at the core of how we serve customers, especially as severe weather becomes more frequent,” said Quates. “We’re building on the progress we’ve made, improving our grid and training our teams so we can respond quickly and safely when severe weather impacts our communities.” Prepared for hurricane season We take a proactive, year-round approach to storm readiness. Ahead of the 2026 summer storm season, Entergy Mississippi completed a series of actions to strengthen our preparedness, including: Inspecting utility poles regularly and replace damaged or broken poles when necessary Inspecting transmission lines, facilities and power plants in preparation for extreme weather conditions Working proactive maintenance plans throughout the year Completing additional vegetation trimming to reduce tree-related outages Reviewing emergency response plans and positioning crews and equipment Employees also took part in staging center training, logistics and resource management exercises and a companywide hurricane drill that simulated a major storm making landfall. These sessions help reinforce consistent procedures, improve coordination across teams and ensure our workforce is fully prepared before severe weather arrives. Customers should prepare now Customers should take steps to prepare their homes and families for potential hurricane impacts. Entergy’s Storm Center website provides guidance on building an emergency plan, assembling a disaster supply kit and safely operating backup generators. Customers are also encouraged to download the Entergy mobile app and sign up for outage text alerts to stay informed during severe weather. Before storms strike, customers can also verify contact information on myEntergy.com , so they receive our notifications. Customers can report an outage quickly and easily through our digital options – using either our free mobile app , online at myEntergy.com or by texting OUT to 36778. “Hurricanes can be unpredictable. We are committed to strengthening the grid and preparing our teams – but preparation is a shared responsibility,” said Quates. “When our customers take steps to prepare early, we are all better positioned to weather any storm.” About Entergy Mississippi Entergy Mississippi provides electricity to approximately 459,000 customers in 45 counties. Entergy Mississippi is a subsidiary of Entergy Corporation. Entergy generates, transmits and distributes electricity to power life for more than 3 million customers through our operating companies in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. We’re focused on keeping costs for our customers as low as possible while providing reliable energy that our communities count on. We’re also investing in growth for the future with a more resilient, cleaner energy system that includes modern natural gas, nuclear and renewable energy generation. As a nationally recognized leader in sustainability and corporate citizenship, we deliver more than $100 million in economic benefits each year to the communities we serve through philanthropy, volunteerism and advocacy. Entergy is a Fortune 500 company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, and has approximately 12,000 employees. Learn more at EntergyMississippi.com and connect with @EntergyMS on social media. Media inquiries: [email protected]

title: Turning threat intelligence into decisive action with Defender Experts
summary: Security teams have never had more visibility, yet rarely have they felt more uncertain. Signal pours in from endpoints, identities, cloud workloads, and a sprawling mix of third-party tools.
body_text: Security teams have never had more visibility, yet rarely have they felt more uncertain. Signal pours in from endpoints, identities, cloud workloads, and a sprawling mix of third-party tools. Dashboards are full, alerts keep coming, but the hardest question of the day remains unanswered: of everything happening right now, what actually matters to us , and what do we do about i t? That space between knowing a threat exists and acting on it is the intelligence-to-action gap, and it’s where most breaches are won or lost. It doesn’t close with another feed or another dashboard. It closes with expertise: seasoned defenders who know your environment, interpret what global signal means for your risk, and stay with you from the first indicator to the final response. Today we’re announcing a new service, Microsoft Defender Experts Threat Intelligence , and we are expanding Microsoft Defender Experts MDR to include new third-party and multi-cloud coverage. Together, these human-led offerings are designed to close the intelligence-to-action gap at the two moments that decide the outcome: before a campaign reaches you, and as it moves through your environment. Upstream: See the campaign before it reaches you The earlier you see a campaign forming, the more options you have, and the cheaper every decision becomes. Yet most threat intelligence still arrives as raw feeds or static reports: high in volume, low in context, and disconnected from what’s exposed in your estate. Teams end up with more to read and no more clarity on what to do about it. Microsoft Defender Experts Threat Intelligence is a new, expert-delivered service that closes that distance. Built on Microsoft’s visibility across endpoints, identity, cloud, and evolving attacker activity, it gives your team periodic, curated insight into the threats most likely to target you. Designated Microsoft experts interpret the global landscape through the lens of your industry, geography, and environment, then translate it into clear, prioritized guidance your team can act on. As campaigns evolve, experts continuously refine that guidance with newly observed infrastructure, tactics, and targeting patterns, helping your team adjust hunting, hardening, and response activities. The insight is tailored for both leadership and defenders, providing executive-ready context alongside technical recommendations so the entire organization can act from a shared understanding of the threat landscape. The goal is simple: help you reduce risk before an attack reaches your environment, not explain what happened after the fact. In practice, your team receives: Early-warning alerts on emerging campaigns relevant to you Campaign-evolution updates as activity unfolds Contextualized intelligence tied to your risk profile Recurring briefings from your designated expert, rotating across geopolitical, industry, and global perspectives, on a scheduled basis In your environment: Follow the threat everywhere it moves Modern attacks rarely stay in one place. They cross from email to endpoint to identity to cloud, and increasingly traverse disparate security tools. Even when organizations have visibility into those environments, connecting multi-vendor and multi-domain signals into a coherent attack story remains a challenge. That’s the gap we’re closing on the response side: Microsoft Defender Experts MDR (formerly Microsoft Defender Experts for XDR) is expanding with new third-party and multi-cloud coverage powered by Microsoft Sentinel. Defender Experts MDR provides a fully managed detection and response service that reduces noise, adds expert context, and drives action. With support for leading non-Microsoft sources across cloud, identity, email, network, and endpoint environments, our experts can follow attacks wherever they move, not just where Microsoft products operate. title: Mueller® provides solutions for quality drinking water
summary: Mueller® provides solutions for quality drinking waterMueller’s portfolio of brands provides extensive solutions to help cities provide safe drinking water and, when used together, help increase water quality. These products help cities and utilities to better prepare for the future and be proactive instead of reactive, and increase efficiency and potentially save money.The
body_text: Date: 04/01/2026 Publication: The Municipal Mueller® provides solutions for quality drinking water Mueller’s portfolio of brands provides extensive solutions to help cities provide safe drinking water and, when used together, help increase water quality. These products help cities and utilities to better prepare for the future and be proactive instead of reactive, and increase efficiency and potentially save money. The Hydro-Guard® connected flushing system helps move water through a distribution network when there is not enough demand to turn the water over, preventing it from aging in the line. At the dead end of a line, water can stagnate if there is not enough movement. On larger lines, there are often not enough homes or businesses to move fresh disinfected water to the dead-end points. An automatic flusher can be used to address these situations where standard demand is insufficient for maintaining a consistent water turnover rate. The flusher can be programmed to flush water lines once a week, daily, for a few minutes a day or for an hour a day. Turning the water over helps manage disinfectant byproduct levels in the lines. Bringing better, disinfected water to customers helps increase water quality and provides safer drinking water. One such case is Liberty Lake in Washington state that used the Hydro-Guard 100 series to address an E.coli discovery by a resident in its waterline before Thanksgiving. Water operators discovered the contamination was from three dead-end lines that were not adequately flushed during daily use, and due to fall sprinkler blow-outs, E. coli entered part of the water supply. Three custom Hydro-Guard automatic flushing systems with water quality sampling stations were installed by Mueller in just one day. Operators programmed automatic flushing of the dead-end lines weekly, and the sampling stations went into position within 18 inches from the flushing systems to ensure an accurate sample was collected. This allowed Liberty Lake residents to get the “all clear” for clean water the day before Thanksgiving. Hydro-Guard has different flushing solutions for different environmental conditions. For warmer climates the system can discharge flushed water to the ground, or it can be discharged directly to a storm pond, sewer, swale, or other discharge point. For cold climates, there are models that can discharge flushed water to the ground, or the discharge can be directed to a dedicated point, such as a pond or storm sewer. Mueller’s FC300 is one option for cold climates. The only part of this flushing unit above ground is a manhole cover, all flushing is below ground. This system is constructed using the Mueller Thermal-Coil® meter box with an integrated meter yoke in addition to the flushing system. This design allows it to be lowered below the frost depth to protect it from freezing and also be worked on above ground when necessary. The most common bury depth for areas with cooler temperatures is between 36 and 84 inches deep. Another water quality device from Hydro-Guard is the sampling station. The Connected Sample Stations also allow water utilities to monitor water pressure and temperature from the sample location. The valve opens and a water sample is collected, and a digital record is created when each sample is taken. If something in the water tests positive, public works employees can go back and see when the sample was taken and check the corresponding water temperature and pressure to determine what is causing the condition. “Unique to Mueller is the design in connectivity between the flushing system and the sampling station,” Harold Mosley, Mueller territory sales manager, described. “Not all flushers have it, but they all have the ability to have it. The sampling station integrates a pressure logger that monitors the distribution of water temperature and pressure. When it comes to water quality, water temperature is a factor. High temperatures have a significant effect on chlorine in the line,” Mosley added. A logger in a flushing system consistently measures temperature. With remote access, an employee can log in and program flushing during a specific timeframe to bring cooler water through the lines. This is important in regions with warm temperatures and shallow water lines. Recently, Decatur, Ill., installed 19 Hydro-Guard blow-off sampling stations at critical points throughout the utility’s distribution network. The move helped eliminate the need to coordinate access to buildings and saved approximately five minutes of flushing per sampling location. Now the city collects samples at optimal times without scheduling conflicts because of a connection right at the water main. During installation, Decatur also added 13 Mueller pressure loggers at the extremities of the system, in high demand areas and at pressure zone boundaries. The system gives information to operators in real time so they can troubleshoot pressure issues and monitor freezing conditions. Over the next several years, the city plans to install an additional 60 sampling stations as well as integrate pressure loggers into the sampling stations. Pressure monitoring and management systems maintain adequate pressure throughout the distribution system. Thresholds can be set and the system can send an alert if it goes too high or too low. This allows operators to see trends and determine the cause of pressure fluctuations. It can also alert staff to a significant pressure drop, indicating a break in the system, so personnel can quickly be dispatched to fix the issue. A control valve is often set and then forgotten for years. “But demand is not static, it is always changing,” Mosley explained. Using an advanced pilot valve that can learn the peak and off-peak operational times of a distribution network, reduces the risk of over pressurizing a water line, which can lead to leaks or line breaks. By optimization pressure in the system, utilities can also reduce operational costs related to pumping. The advanced pilot valve dials the pressure back during off-peak hours and dials the pressure up when necessary. It relies on the pressure monitoring system to actuate it and understand what the system needs and when it needs it. This lowers energy costs by not over-pumping. It also gives health reports on the control valve. If the pressure bounces around on the trend map, the control valve may need some work. The Echologics® leak detection system helps to find leaks with constant monitoring . If a leak is detected that information is relayed to the utility. This leak detection system can find very small leaks, helping utilities to prioritize repair and avoid major breaks and disruptions. “The real value in Mueller’s approach is that we have a diverse portfolio, and it all plays well together,” Mosley stressed.

title: How to Create a Will: Your Estate Planning Guide
summary: Ready to create a will but not sure where to start? This guide will help you identify your needs—and when it’s time to talk to an attorney.
body_text: Step 2: Designate beneficiaries and inheritance details Beneficiaries are the people who will receive your hard-earned assets. Without clear beneficiary designations, your assets might end up in the hands of distant relatives or distributed by the probate court according to state law. To prevent this, ensure your beneficiary designations are current, including any tangible assets such as personal property. Being specific can help avoid potential disputes among heirs. Here are some tips for deciding who should inherit your assets: Name a primary and a contingent beneficiary. Life is ever-changing. It’'s good to have a contingent beneficiary in your will if something happens to your primary beneficiary or you simply change your mind about where you want your assets to go. Update your will for life events. Review your list of beneficiaries regularly. Significant life changes like births, deaths, divorces, and marriages are good times to review your will and to update your beneficiaries as needed. Be mindful of tax consequences. Some things that can be transferred by beneficiary designation, like IRAs, retirement plans, and life insurance policies, have specific tax rules. Awareness of tax rules will help ensure you leave your beneficiaries your assets, not tax debt. Step 3: Appoint guardians to minor children Selecting trusted guardians who share your values and will care for your children responsibly is an important part of creating a will. It can also prevent possible probate court disputes. When picking a legal guardian, consider their willingness and responsibility. You can also specify in your will a person you do not wish to have guardianship of your children, ensuring the kids’ best interests are always prioritized. Here are some things to think about when appointing a guardian for your minor children: Skills. Choose a guardian you feel will be good with and good to your children—someone with the time and disposition to care for and nurture your children. Shared values. Choose a guardian you and your children know well and are comfortable with—someone who shares your values and parenting style. If you have any specific religious beliefs, choose a guardian who shares your faith. Financial stability. Even if you plan to leave something behind to help with the care and upbringing of your children, you should choose a financially stable guardian. Your guardian should be someone who can feed, clothe, and educate your children without it being a financial burden. Physical ability. A person who may become your child’s guardian should be someone who can shepherd your child through to adulthood and is healthy enough to handle the challenges of parenthood. Willingness. Before you designate a guardian for your minor children, ask the potential guardian if they are willing to care for your children. Backup guardians. You should have at least one backup guardian for your children. If anything happens to the first guardian, this ensures you still have someone to care for your children.

title: Dayvigo Side Effects: A Comprehensive Guide to Potential Risks and Impacts
summary: Explore a comprehensive guide to Dayvigo side effects, unraveling potential risks and impacts for informed decision-making. Dive into our detailed insights
body_text: Persistent sleep troubles can make nights feel endless. Dayvigo is a modern solution for better sleep, but it's important to know it comes with potential side effects. Dr. Shiyan Yeo, Internal Medicine Physician, Sleep Medicine Expert: “Some patients report grogginess, confusion, or abnormal dreams—side effects that should be monitored closely.” Take the first step towards improving your sleep with Sleep Reset. Start by taking our sleep quiz , enabling us to pinpoint your key issues. Following the quiz, opt to work with your personal sleep coach and gain access to our dedicated sleep program. It's a proactive approach to address sleep concerns without the risks associated with medications like Dayvigo. Understanding Dayvigo Dayvigo, known generically as lemborexant, is a prescription medication tailored for the treatment of insomnia . It characterizes a novel class of sleep aids, distinct in its mechanism of action. As an orexin receptor antagonist, Dayvigo operates by hindering neurotransmitter activity that typically sustains wakefulness. Through this targeted inhibition, it facilitates the onset and maintenance of sleep. The term "orexin receptor antagonist" underscores Dayvigo's engagement with specific brain receptors to exert its sedative effect, marking a precise pharmacological intervention. Medication Overview Dayvigo is a prescription medication formulated to treat insomnia , particularly difficulties in initiating and maintaining sleep. Its efficacy has been demonstrated through rigorous clinical trials. Lemborexant, the active compound in Dayvigo, operates by inhibiting the orexin neurotransmission pathway, which plays a pivotal role in regulating the sleep-wake cycle. The medication's unique mechanism provides targeted intervention. Lemborexant has shown a reduction in sleep latency and improved sleep maintenance. While Dayvigo offers potential benefits for insomnia sufferers, it's crucial to be aware of its side effect profile. Ranging from mild to severe, reported adverse effects include somnolence, fatigue, and complex sleep behaviors, underscoring the importance of physician guidance in its use. Common Usage and Dosage Dayvigo (lemborexant) is indicated for the treatment of insomnia in adults, facilitating the ease of falling and staying asleep. Initial Dose : Typically, the starting dose is 5 mg, taken orally, once per night. Maintenance Dose : Depending on efficacy and tolerability, the dose can be increased to a maximum of 10 mg per night. Administration Timing : It should be taken immediately before bedtime, with at least 7 hours remaining before the planned time of awakening. Use with Food : Dayvigo may be taken with or without food, however, a high-fat meal may reduce its efficacy. Special Populations : Dosage adjustments may be required for elderly patients, those with liver impairment, or those taking inhibitors of P-gp or CYP3A4 enzymes. A suitable dosage regimen is pivotal to balance efficacy with safety, and should be individualized. Adherence to the prescribed dosage is crucial to mitigate potential risks and optimize the therapeutic benefits of Dayvigo. Mild to Moderate Side Effects When considering the potential adverse effects of Dayvigo, mild to moderate side effects may include drowsiness, headache, and dizziness. These symptoms are relatively common and could present as transient episodes shortly after commencing the medication. Other symptoms such as fatigue, somnolence, and dry mouth may also be observed in certain individuals, although they generally do not necessitate discontinuation of therapy. It is essential for patients to report any persistent or bothersome side effects to their healthcare provider for assessment. While most of these reactions can be managed with dose adjustments or symptomatic treatment, ongoing monitoring is important. Some people may experience an alteration in their sleep-wake cycle or changes in mood, which should be carefully evaluated to ensure that the benefits of Dayvigo continue to outweigh any potential negative impacts on quality of life. Sleep-Related Symptoms Dayvigo may induce complex sleep behaviors. While primarily prescribed to alleviate insomnia, Dayvigo has been associated with sleep-related adverse effects. The potential for sleepwalking, sleep-driving, and engaging in other activities while not fully awake is a concern requiring vigilance. Consequently, patients must be monitored for unusual sleep-related behaviors, which could pose personal harm or safety concerns. Abrupt cessation may exacerbate sleep disturbances. Patients who abruptly discontinue Dayvigo may experience withdrawal symptoms or a rebound in insomnia severity. Therefore, it is critical to follow a healthcare provider's guidance when discontinuing use - to avoid abrupt cessation and ensure a gradual tapering schedule to mitigate potential sleep-related withdrawal effects. Risk of increased daytime sleepiness or fatigue. Individuals taking Dayvigo might encounter excessive daytime drowsiness or lethargy as a side effect. Continuous assessment and tailoring of dosage are advisable if such symptoms present, as these can interfere with daily functioning and personal safety, particularly with activities such as driving or operating machinery. Gastrointestinal Disturbances Among the side effects associated with Dayvigo, gastrointestinal issues rank prominently, presenting symptoms such as nausea, constipation, or diarrhea. Both the frequency and severity of such side effects warrant consideration when assessing patient response to this medication. Nausea is a commonly cited side effect linked to Dayvigo. Its onset can vary among individuals and may affect daily activities and appetite. Constipation, another side effect, can significantly impact a patient's comfort and quality of life. The involvement of serotonin receptors (which are implicated in gut motility) may partially explain this adverse effect. Diarrhea, while less common than constipation, may also occur in patients taking Dayvigo. This can lead to dehydration and electrolyte imbalances, necessitating close monitoring and possible intervention. In addition to these primary concerns, some individuals may experience abdominal pain or discomfort. These symptoms can be distressing and impact the overall therapeutic experience, influencing the decision to continue or adjust treatment with Dayvigo. Lastly, it is crucial to assess each patient's unique gastrointestinal profile before initiating Dayvigo therapy. Prior history of digestive issues should be considered, as pre-existing conditions may exacerbate these side effects. Mood and Behavioral Changes Lemborexant, the active ingredient in Dayvigo, can sometimes influence mood. Individuals may report feeling uncharacteristically irritable or agitated after initiating treatment. Caution is advised, as some patients may experience noticeable changes in affect, presenting symptoms such as sadness or emotional blunting. These mood alterations could potentially impact interpersonal relationships and daily functioning. Furthermore, there is a palpable risk of more serious mood disturbances, such as depressive symptoms or anxiety. It is essential for clinicians to monitor patients closely for any indications of such changes, especially during the early stages of treatment. Behavioral changes, including sleepwalking or other complex sleep-related behaviors, have been observed with Dayvigo. These behaviors occur without consciousness and can lead to potential harm, making safety measures a necessary discussion point in patient counseling. Clinicians should remain vigilant for any signs of mood or behavioral alterations. Swift intervention may be required to mitigate these potential risks associated with Dayvigo therapy. Severe Adverse Reactions In the landscape of potential side effects, there is a subset of severe adverse reactions that warrant immediate medical attention. Among these, anaphylaxis and other hypersensitivity reactions have been reported, albeit rarely. Such reactions are medical emergencies, characterized by symptoms including difficulty breathing, severe rash, and swelling of the face or throat. Physicians must advise patients of the signs of a severe allergic reaction to Dayvigo and the importance of prompt intervention. Complex sleep behaviors , such as sleep-driving, which can occur without alertness or recall, also present serious safety risks and necessitate urgent evaluation and potentially discontinuation of the medication. Neurological sequelae , including amnesia and anxiety , may also manifest and can profoundly impact a patient's cognitive and psychological well-being. It is crucial that healthcare providers consistently screen for these adverse reactions and approach prescribed treatment plans with a judicious balance of therapeutic benefit and risk assessment. Allergic Reactions and Anaphylaxis Dr. Michael Grandner, Sleep Expert, Professor of Neuroscience and Physiological Sciences: “Like all sleep medications, Dayvigo should be used with caution and only under medical supervision.” Allergic reactions to Dayvigo, while uncommon, can be severe and potentially life-threatening. Immediate skin reactions: Signs such as hives, itching, or rash warrant prompt attention. Respiratory distress: Difficulty breathing or wheezing is indicative of a serious reaction. Gastrointestinal disturbances: Nausea or vomiting may accompany other allergic symptoms. Cardiovascular implications: Rapid heartbeat or feeling faint could signal a severe response. Angioedema: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat requires immediate medical intervention. Patients should seek emergency treatment if they experience symptoms of anaphylaxis. Early recognition and management of allergic reactions are critical to prevent severe outcomes. Complex Sleep Behaviors Dayvigo may induce complex sleep behaviors that can lead to potential injury. Sleepwalking: Engaging in activities while not fully awake. Sleep-driving: Operating a vehicle with no memory of the event afterward. Use of machinery: Handling machinery or appliances without full consciousness. Preparing and eating food: Making and consuming food without recalling the activity. Having sex: Initiating a sexual encounter without any recollection later. Such behaviors require immediate discontinuation of Dayvigo. By their very nature, complex sleep behaviors are dangerous and surreptitious. The absence of memory for such events underscores the importance of pre-screening patients for risk factors. Long-term Usage Considerations Long-term use of Dayvigo should be approached with caution, as the prospect of dependency, tolerance, or withdrawal symptoms cannot be entirely discounted. Over time, patients may notice a diminution in therapeutic efficacy, prompting a reevaluation of treatment strategies that could involve dose adjustments or a transition to alternative therapies. It is pivotal to engage in periodic clinical reviews to ensure the sustained suitability and safety of Dayvigo for each individual. Regular monitoring for potential side effects is essential when Dayvigo is used over extended periods. Concerns particularly arise regarding cognitive function, such as memory impairment or altered alertness, which may impact daily activities. As the pharmacologic profile of Dayvigo necessitates vigilance, continuous dialogue between healthcare professionals and patients plays a critical role in managing long-term treatment. Dependence Potential Dayvigo (lemborexant) possesses inherent properties associated with risks of dependence, often manifesting with prolonged use. As with other medications acting on the central nervous system, patterns of sustained consumption could lead to physical or psychological reliance. Such outcomes necessitate circumspect prescribing and vigilant patient oversight. Despite the relatively lower propensity for dependence with Dayvigo compared to benzodiazepines, caution is warranted. Recognizing early signs of tolerance is vital in mitigating the onset of dependence. Notably, abrupt cessation after extended Dayvigo use may result in withdrawal symptoms. Hence, a gradual tapering approach (advised under medical supervision) is prudent when discontinuing therapy. The propensity for dependence often escalates in concordance with dosage and duration of treatment. Expert guidelines suggest deploying the lowest effective dose and reassessing the need for continued therapy at regular intervals to mitigate this risk. Patients with a history of substance abuse or addiction should approach Dayvigo with exceptional caution, and in such cases, alternative therapeutic options might be more advisable to reduce potential risks. Ultimately, a diligent assessment of each patient's individual risk profile is critical. Thorough, ongoing dialogue between healthcare providers and patients can ensure that Dayvigo's benefits consistently outweigh the risks associated with dependence. Withdrawal and Discontinuation Effects Upon discontinuation, patients may experience withdrawal symptoms reflective of Dayvigo's CNS depressant effects. Withdrawal symptoms, while generally mild to moderate, may manifest in various forms; insomnia resurgence, anxiety, agitation, and irritability are amongst the most commonly reported. Balancing symptom management with gradual dose reduction is paramount in mitigating withdrawal effects. Healthcare providers should closely monitor patients during this period to adjust the tapering schedule as needed. Gradual reduction of Dayvigo, rather than sudden cessation, is recommended to allow for the patient's neurochemistry to adapt to the absence of the drug. An abrupt halt in therapy can lead to rebound insomnia, where the initial sleep difficulty that led to Dayvigo treatment may temporarily worsen. In the landscape of pharmacological sleep aids, withdrawal and discontinuation effects are an essential consideration. Special care should be taken in planning the discontinuation process to prevent withdrawal symptoms, which in turn may influence the patient's quality of life and psychological well-being. It is incumbent upon both prescriber and patient to approach the cessation of Dayvigo with a strategic, informed, and personalized plan, cognizant of the medication's pharmacodynamic properties and the unique physiological responses of the individual. title: U.S. Army Awards Rune Technologies $2M for Predictive Logistics Platform
summary: Direct to Phase II SBIR contract will deploy Rune’s TyrOS software with elements of the 1st Cavalry Division
body_text: ARLINGTON, Va., March 12, 2026 - Rune Technologies, which builds AI-enabled predictive software for military logistics in contested environments, today announced a $2 million Direct to Phase II Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contract from the U.S. Army. This award supports the Army's PORTAL (Predict, Optimize, Recommend, and Track for Adaptive Logistics) program through the Army Applications Laboratory (AAL) in association with Army FUZE. Over the next 18 months, Rune will partner with the 1st Cavalry Division, based in Fort Hood, Texas, to deploy its TyrOS platform across multiple echelons. The system will replace legacy manual processes, which has already demonstrated its resilience and efficacy in exercises with the 25th Infantry Division, 4th Infantry Division, XVIII Airborne Corps, and even the 1st Cavalry Division in a separate engagement. These stress tests are important milestones in developing measurable improvements in sustainment speed, accuracy, and decision quality. The PORTAL program addresses a critical need in modern military operations: logistics systems that can function when communications are denied, disrupted, intermittent, or limited. Traditional logistics systems struggle to integrate data from disparate Army platforms and cannot operate effectively when adversaries target supply lines and communications infrastructure. TyrOS addresses this issue through an edge-first architecture that embeds intelligence directly at the tactical level, enabling units to track assets, predict potential shortfalls, and receive optimized courses of action without requiring constant connectivity. "The Army faces increasingly complex logistics challenges as near-peer adversaries develop capabilities to disrupt traditional supply chains," said David Tuttle, Co-Founder and CEO of Rune Technologies. "This contract validates our approach of building software that works at the tactical edge, where decisions get made, rather than relying on distant servers that become unavailable in contested environments. We're honored to support the Army's efforts to maintain logistics superiority in any operational scenario." The Direct to Phase II designation recognizes that Rune's predictive logistics technology has already achieved sufficient feasibility. The SBIR contract allows the Army to accelerate adoption by supporting rigorous military testing and integration with existing systems rather than starting from basic research. Under the contract, Rune will refine TyrOS to integrate with existing Army systems, including the Joint Battle Command Platform and Global Combat Support System-Army. This 18-month effort focuses on rigorous field testing with operational units, featuring measurable capabilities that address Army requirements and clear technical milestones. This contract marks another significant milestone for Rune with the Army, which recently became the first company selected by both prime contractor teams on the Army's NGC2 program: Lockheed Martin and Anduril. “We are bringing intelligent planning to Sustainers in the 1st Cavalry Division.” Said SSG Mickey Reeve, program manager for PORTAL. “Rune will be developing their capabilities based on Warfighter feedback during collective training in challenging missions meant to emulate threats of capable adversaries.” The Rune team emphasizes solving problems from the point of need upward rather than imposing enterprise systems on tactical environments, reflecting an edge-first philosophy. This method, coupled with a proven ability to rapidly deliver, validate, and iterate fielded software in collaboration with soldiers, is core to Rune’s approach to technology development. Rune's TyrOS platform transforms manual logistics processes into intelligent supply webs that anticipate needs, optimize resources, and enable distributed operations at machine speed—even when supply lines are targeted by near-peer adversaries. title: What Is B2B Sales Outsourcing and How to Do It Right?
summary: Discover how to outsource B2B sales to professionals and see why Upcall is different.
body_text: tips b2b What Is B2B Sales Outsourcing and How to Do It Right? At its simplest, B2B sales outsourcing has three components, as the name suggests. Firstly, it involves direct connections between businesses. Secondly, it’s a way to maximize sales. And thirdly, it’s a sales method which is “outsourced” to a third party service provider. As such, it’s an alternative to traditional sales systems that exist entirely within companies, and it has plenty of advantages over those older ways of operating. Let’s look at how it works in more detail before moving onto some of the reasons why you might want to give sales outsourcing a try. Capitalize on the Advantages of Outsourcing Your B2B Sales When you outsource sales, that doesn’t mean losing control over the strategic direction of your business and it doesn’t necessarily mean moving your entire sales team over to an external company. But it does mean harnessing the specialist sales expertise of external providers. Sometimes, companies choose to transfer their day-to-day sales operations completely. Others prefer to use outsourcing for individual campaigns, when a little bit more capacity is required and their core team can’t deliver. It can also be employed for specific sales tasks. For example, you could choose to outsource your market research operations, bringing in specialists to research your client base and find out exactly what they want. Conversely, you might wish to move your lead qualification systems to an external provider with expertise in inbound marketing and responsive phone-based sales. And the same applies to both lead conversion and customer relationship management. Thanks to cutting edge outsourcing experts, all of these sales functions can be performed out of house. It’s just a matter of choosing which functions you would prefer to delegate. Using Outsourcing Well Can Have Huge Sales Advantages At first glance, outsourcing might seem intimidating, particularly for small businesses with relatively tight margins and a tradition of keeping close control over sales professionals. But that’s largely a mirage. Much of the time, SMEs find that the benefits of B2B outsourcing outweigh their anxieties about control, providing that outsourcing is done right. Those benefits can be transformative for all kinds of business. For example, if you are branching out into a new product sector or geographical area, outsourcing can bring in local or sector-specific expertise that your core team doesn’t possess. In cases like that, it could be used to hit the ground running fast in an area that you aren’t familiar with, while you train existing staff to hone their knowledge or recruit new permanent staff to fill the gap. Outsourcing your sales operations is also a great way to innovate. Used well, outsourced sales teams can allow companies to try out new ideas before mainstreaming them in their own office. Then there are instances where sales forces stagnate and a stimulus is required. Whether the causes are burnout or the inability to take in new ideas, outsourcing sales functions is often a good way to inject dynamism into your sales operations. Specialist sales companies can bring in agile, up to date ideas about customer liaison, lead qualification and CRM. And if you bring them in on a short-term basis, they can provide a motivation to your own sales team to shape up and improve their performance. Finally, outsourcing can be a wholesale substitute for standard sales structures. If companies are experiencing sluggish sales and their metrics on lead conversion aren’t trending upwards, outsourcing can be an effective solution. In some sectors like real estate, more efficient sales teams can be the key to unlocking regions or retaining customers, and this kind of efficiency is where outsourcing excels. How Can You Introduce A Streamlined B2B Sales Solution? We know that outsourcing sales operations can have huge benefits for a wide variety of SMEs, but there are also dangers when outsourcing is handled poorly. For instance, existing customers might resent dealing with unfamiliar contacts, core sales teams could become demoralized, and managers may lose control over the overall direction of their sales strategy. These are real risks, so outsourcing needs to be done properly. Firstly, it pays to understand which type of businesses are well-suited to outsourcing sales operations. Generally speaking, outsourcing works well when companies have large quantities of incoming leads (such as real estate brokers, vehicle leasing companies, or IT suppliers). And it functions best when these leads need to be dealt with as quickly as possible. So, if you operate in a highly competitive, lead-based sector outsourcing could be the ideal solution. You also need to be clear about the purpose of any outsourcing operation. There’s no sense in duplicating work between core teams and outsourced providers. And there’s no sense in tasking external companies with performing work with a low return. Because of this, it makes sense to audit your sales operation before outsourcing, to understand where external contractors can add value, and tailor your commissioning around those findings. Choose the Right B2B Sales Experts to Enhance Your Business Outsourcing sales operations can be hugely beneficial if you know what you are looking for and understand how it can enhance your bottom line. But there’s another key aspect to the process that needs to be considered: The need to find a partner who is responsive to your needs, will implement your plans faithfully, and who has the skills to deliver. Not all outsourcing companies meet those criteria, so be sure to research your partner thoroughly. Ideally, both you and your outsourcing provider need to have a complete understanding of the task in hand. For example, if you take qualifying leads out-of-house, the external sales representatives need accurate information about your products and how the sales funnel works following initial contact. If not, as customers move on to Account Executives to close the deal, misunderstandings could develop, resulting in poorer lead conversion rates. Everything has to work together, or as closely as possible, making it vital to provide outsourcing companies with high-quality briefs. And your partner needs to be honest about any difficulties that arise. Outsourcing is a process, not a magic spell, and teething problems usually arise. So both sides need to have a strong working relationship. Revolutionize Your Inbound Marketing Systems with Strategic Outsourcing By now, you should have an idea about whether your business meets the criteria for outsourcing sales operations or not. If your sales figures are stagnant, you need to expand confidently, your lead qualification systems are dysfunctional, or you just want to try something new, Upcall could well supply the perfect solution. Upcall specialize in providing teams of “Upcallers” who are experts in handling inbound marketing challenges. As a first point of contact between clients and companies, our teams can field calls and draw customers into sales funnels, qualifying leads diligently before handing them on to your own executives. At the same time, Upcall’s service provides real-time data regarding contacts and leads, while delivering efficiency gains below the cost of a full-time sales employee. Whether you need a temporary solution or a long-term replacement for your sales staff, help is at hand. Outsourcing could be the way forward, and Upcall are ready to help you take the first steps. title: How to brief AI creative tools, a framework for marketing teams
summary: Master how to brief AI creative tools to get more accurate, on-brand results with a practical framework and real prompt examples.
body_text: TL;DR AI creative tools are only as good as the brief behind them, yet most teams still prompt them like a search box and blame the tool when the results come back generic. This is a practical framework for briefing AI the way you brief a creative team: a reusable nine-part structure, tool-by-tool guidance for the five tools marketing teams use most and the point where prompting alone stops scaling. That's where Brand Brain and Superside's human-led, AI-first model take over. Imagine telling a designer, "create a great ad" without any context. No notes on the target audience, product or brand standards. If the result misses the mark, you wouldn't blame the designer, would you? You'd blame the brief. Yet that's exactly how many enterprise marketing teams use AI. Someone opens a tool, types "create an ad for our new product," and gets a disappointing result. They tweak the prompt, try again and get more of the same. The verdict: AI is overhyped. Here's what many marketing teams still miss. A prompt is a brief. AI simply follows your instructions, and if you give it vague input, the output will be generic. That's why teams that brief AI the way they brief their creatives consistently outperform those that still write prompts like search queries. The good news? Learning how to prompt AI for marketing involves many of the same briefing principles marketing teams already use. But there are a few twists. This article shares a practical, reusable framework for how to brief AI creative tools, along with tool-specific tips and real AI prompts for marketing teams that want to nail AI creative briefing. AI prompts are creative briefing in a new form Every experienced marketing leader has suffered the cost of a bad creative brief. Unclear instructions lead to work that misses the mark. Then countless revision rounds and frustrating creative bottlenecks follow. This scenario is, in fact, so common that only 10% of creative professionals feel they're briefed well. On the other hand, 80% of marketers believe their briefs are on-point. This gap between what marketers think they've communicated and what creatives actually receive is where projects start to go off track. AI, unfortunately, only amplifies the problem. Instead of producing a single poor result from a vague brief, the AI tool happily produces hundreds of off-brand outputs within minutes. If there's one thing you remember after reading this article, it's this: one-liner prompts simply don't work in enterprise creative environments. A request like "give me 10 creative ideas for our new campaign" gives the AI tool zilch to work with. Much like a creative team needs a proper brief to produce good work, AI needs a strong prompt, written by a human, to produce good output. Catalina Jimenez CPM Team Lead at Superside Instead, humans must do the thinking first and then share sufficient information on the audience, customer pain points, past campaign successes, brand tone of voice and more as part of a solid creative brief that determines the quality of everything that follows. When the brief is vague, AI produces generic outputs. But when you share a strong brief, AI can produce high-quality , on-brand work. I'm the brain and AI is the hands. What I focus on is being very precise about what I need, how I need it and how I frame it. Cristian Ginori Marketing Strategy Manager at Superside An important part of the process is to match the creative brief to the right phase of production: During ideation , prioritize exploration over precision. Give the tool enough context to generate a wide range of ideas, then refine the strongest directions. During production , shift from possibilities to precision. Include detailed guidelines, specs, guardrails and references so the final asset is as close to perfect as possible. This approach mirrors the logic of Superside's six- phase AI creative framework for performance marketing: explore ideas first, then refine and test them. The anatomy of a great AI creative brief A good AI brief contains the same information you'd give a human creative, organized in a way that AI can easily interpret. Use the nine-part AI brief framework below as a reusable template, and run through it for every brief to avoid missing details that can weaken the output: Role and context: Tell the AI tool what its role is, and the situation, like "you're a senior B2B copywriter for a fintech brand launching a new feature." Objective: Share the asset's job, in business terms. Not "create an ad," but "create an ad that makes risk leaders curious enough to book a demo." Audience: Tell the tool who the ad is for, beyond demographics. Think role, pain points, beliefs or what would stop the target customer mid-scroll. Core message: Share the one thing you want the audience to remember. Brand guardrails: Specify voice and tone, visual style, colors, logo rules, a list of explicit don'ts and any other important info. This is where most off-brand AI output is prevented or created. Format and specs: Clarify the channel, dimensions, aspect ratios, length and file type. Is the asset a LinkedIn feed image, a 30-second vertical video for Meta or a 150-character headline? Be specific. References: Include examples of the style and mood you're after, and what you don't want. "Like this, not that" is the single most powerful input for visual AI tools. Constraints: Specify must-include and must-avoid elements. Think required legal language, banned claims, competitor names to avoid and accessibility requirements. Output: Tell the tool exactly what you want it to produce, and how many versions you need, like "10 headline options and three visual concepts." Now, let's take the B2B fintech product example and see what a full prompt would look like: Prompt You're a senior B2B copywriter for a fintech brand launching a new feature. Objective: create a LinkedIn ad that gets risk and fraud leaders at mid-market banks to book a demo of our new AI fraud-detection feature. Audience: skeptical, risk-averse heads of fraud who have been burned by overhyped tools. Core message: catch fraud earlier, with fewer false positives, without adding headcount. Brand voice: confident, precise, no hype, no jargon. Visual style: clean, modern, deep navy with one electric-green accent, real-feeling, not stock. Format: 1080x1080, headline under 10 words plus one supporting line. Constraints: no fake statistics, no images of literal padlocks or hooded hackers. Output: five headline-and-visual-concept pairs I can choose from. How to brief the five AI creative tools marketing teams use most Next, we'll explore how the AI brief framework can be applied to the tools your team already uses. The framework stays the same, no matter which AI tool you use (it can also brief human creatives). What changes is how you tailor the brief for the most popular AI creative tools. 1. ChatGPT (OpenAI) for copy, concepts and first-draft briefs Best for: ideation, copywriting, messaging variations and audience analysis. It can also be the text workhorse for drafting the briefs you'll feed other tools. How to brief: assign it a role, provide the full project context and ask for a specific number of options in a specific format. ChatGPT rewards iteration, so treat the first outputs as a starting point and then refine them. Ask the tool to make the next outputs punchier, more skeptical and more on-brand. Paste in your actual brand voice guidelines and past high-performing copy so it matches your voice, not the internet's. Sample prompt: "You're a senior B2B copywriter for a confident, no-hype fintech brand. Here are our voice guidelines and three past ads that performed well [paste]. Write 10 LinkedIn headlines under 10 words for our AI fraud-detection launch, aimed at skeptical heads of fraud. The message: catch fraud earlier with fewer false positives. Avoid hype words and jargon. Return them as a numbered list with a one-line rationale each." Common pitfall: accepting the first answer. The first response gives you the average, while the gold comes from refinement. Also always fact-check anything ChatGPT states as a statistic, since these are often fabrications. 2. Midjourney for premium, stylized visual concepts Best for: high-quality, art-directed imagery and visual exploration. Midjourney excels at producing mood boards, concepting and hero visuals. How to brief: image tools work best with a clear description of the scene and a few technical details. Avoid long prose explaining your strategy. Lead with subject and composition, then style, lighting and mood, and lastly technical parameters like aspect ratio. Use reference images to anchor the look, and use negative parameters to exclude what you don't want. Keep the strategy in your head and translate it into visual language. Sample prompt: "Create an editorial photo of a calm fraud analyst in a modern bank office, studying a clean fraud-detection dashboard, minimalist workspace, deep navy and electric-green color palette, soft natural window light, premium editorial photography, shot on 35mm film, shallow depth of field, clean composition --ar 1:1 --style raw --no padlocks, hooded figures, binary code, clutter." Common pitfall: writing Midjourney prompts like ChatGPT prompts. Midjourney needs vivid, concrete visual direction and references rather than objective or audience-focused prompts. Bonus tip: keep brand specifics like exact hex colors for the human finishing pass, since Midjourney approximates rather than matches them precisely. 3. Adobe Firefly for brand-safe, production-ready imagery Best for: enterprise teams with strict legal and brand requirements, as Adobe Firefly 's own models are trained on licensed and public-domain content. It's the tool to reach for when an asset is going live and the brand and legal stakes are high. How to brief: start with the same visual description you'd use for Midjourney, then reinforce it with your brand guardrails. Sample prompt: "Create an editorial photo of a calm fraud analyst in a modern bank office, studying a clean fraud-detection dashboard, minimalist workspace, deep navy and electric-green color palette, soft natural window light, premium editorial photography." Then apply your uploaded brand reference images, style references, color palette and any typography or composition controls available in Firefly. Common pitfall: assuming the asset is ready to ship because brand guardrails were supplied. A human still needs to verify it adheres to your brand guidelines, meets legal and compliance requirements and communicates the right message. 4. Runway for AI video and motion Best for: social content, video teasers and bringing static visuals to life. Runway excels at cinematic motion. How to brief: think like a director, not a copywriter. Describe the shot: subject, action, camera movement, pacing and mood, one scene at a time. Vague prompts produce vague, uncanny motion, so be specific about what should move and how. Generate short clips, choose the best and plan for human editing to assemble and polish the final asset. Sample prompt: "A slow push-in on a clean data dashboard in a modern bank office, subtle UI elements animating as a fraud alert resolves to green. Calm and confident mood, soft depth of field, 6 seconds, no text." Then iterate per scene. Common pitfall: expecting a finished asset from one prompt. Video is the area where human editing, sound and brand finishing matter most. Use Runway to generate raw material, not final cuts. 5. Google Gemini, the multimodal workhorse Best for: multimodal work that combines text, images and analysis. Google Gemini can analyze documents, brand guidelines and references, then generate or refine assets based on that context. How to brief: take advantage of the multimodality. Upload competitor ads, your own brand guidelines and past creative. Then ask Gemini to analyze what your competitors do and brief against them. Give it clear documents to ground its answers rather than relying on its general knowledge. Sample prompt: "Attached are our brand guidelines, our last campaign and three competitor fraud-detection ads. Summarize the visual and messaging conventions of the category, then give me three campaign territories that feel distinct from competitors but consistent with our brand, with a sample headline and visual direction for each." Common pitfall: using Gemini as a generic chatbot. Instead, use it to reason over the specific material you give it. Feed it your real inputs, or you get the same averaged output as everywhere else. Where prompting alone hits a wall for enterprises These techniques will improve anyone's AI prompting. But if you're part of an enterprise team, prompting alone will only get you so far. The first hurdle is brand consistency at scale . A well-written prompt can produce a great asset. But it can't guarantee that the next creative on your team, or in another market, will get the same on-brand result . Because generic AI tools don't remember your brand, every prompt starts from scratch. Small differences in how people describe the brand eventually lead to large-scale brand drift. The second hurdle is a lack of expertise in prompting. Each AI tool works differently, which means marketing teams need to learn distinct prompting techniques for each. That's manageable on a small scale. But expecting every team member across a large organization to become an expert at prompt engineering isn't realistic. The third hurdle is governance. While it's easy to generate content with AI, it's much harder to ensure the AI creative is accurate, on-brand, compliant and ready to publish . At enterprise scale, every AI-generated asset still needs to be reviewed by humans to ensure brand, legal and quality standards are met. The stakes are simply too high. The fourth hurdle is tool sprawl. When teams have to constantly move between platforms, it wastes time and energy. Before long, managing the tools starts eating into the efficiency gains AI was supposed to bring . The bottom line: past a certain scale, a good creative brief is necessary, but it's not enough. Enterprise marketing teams also need systems that carry the brand, bridge the prompting expertise gap, consolidate the tools and help deliver high-quality, on-brand work at speed. A capable system runs KYC (Know Your Customer) identity verification during onboarding, supports just-in-time funding , and files 1099s at year-end without manual input. It also collects W-9s (US tax identification forms) from domestic contractors and W-8BENs (foreign status certification forms) from international payees, then validates each Taxpayer Identification Number against IRS records before any payout clears. Tools that skip these steps push the compliance burden back onto your team. How We Ranked These Contractor Payment Solutions Finding the right contractor payment solution law firm leaders need requires clear criteria. We ranked these vendors using publicly available documentation, not internal software tests. Recent lawyer industry statistics show legal practices increasingly rely on outside experts, and as that contractor volume grows, the gaps in generic payout tools become harder to absorb: slow settlement, manual tax filing, and patchwork compliance all compound. We scored each provider on rail coverage, instant settlement fees, tax automation depth, and global payee reach to surface the options most relevant to legal and professional services firms. Best Overall Contractor Payment Solution: Dots We built Dots as an API for legal and professional services paying contractors at scale. Our tool handles the entire contractor payout lifecycle under a single contract, delivering instant settlement without daily caps. As a contractor payment solution law firm leaders trust, we combine global coverage with strict compliance. Here is what sets our API apart: 300 rails across 190 countries, including the best global payout APIs , via RTP (Real-Time Payments), FedNow, ACH, SWIFT, Venmo, CashApp, and hundreds of local international rails. Payees in the eurozone settle via SEPA Instant in under ten seconds; recipients in Brazil and India clear funds through PIX and UPI. Every payment routes through the lowest-cost rail available for the recipient's jurisdiction, with no extra instant-payout surcharge and no daily volume caps. Stripe Connect Stripe Connect routes funds to connected accounts through a widely recognized API. Many legal teams select this option to route standard disbursements, though there are known Stripe Connect payout gaps worth reviewing. title: What "Agent-Native" Content Infrastructure Actually Means
summary: Everyone is calling their product agent-native. Here is what that term actually requires, what most tools get wrong, and what real AI agent support looks like in a headless CMS.
body_text: The phrase "agent-native" is everywhere right now. Builder.io published a post on it. Vendors are appending it to product descriptions. It is becoming the new "AI-powered" — a term that sounds meaningful until you realize everyone is using it to mean something slightly different. So let's be direct about what agent-native content infrastructure actually requires, where most tools fall short, and what it looks like when an AI agent genuinely operates inside your content stack. What the term is supposed to mean Builder.io's framing is worth engaging with honestly, because parts of it are correct. The core idea: an AI agent that works beside your content (generating copy in a chat window that a human then pastes somewhere) is less useful than an agent that works inside your content system (reading, writing, publishing, and routing for approval directly in the actual CMS). That distinction is real and important. Agents that only produce text blobs for humans to manually process are not materially different from autocomplete. The value compounds when the agent can take action on the real asset, leave a record, and hand off to a human checkpoint before anything ships. Where the framing gets slippery is in what counts as "inside the system." Having an agent that can drop text into a page builder component is not the same as having an agent that operates across your full content model, respects your permissions structure, publishes via your API, and routes through your editorial workflow. What most CMS vendors actually ship When most CMS vendors say "AI," they mean one or more of these: A text generation button inside the editor (autocomplete with a better model) An AI field that suggests values based on other field content A chatbot interface that answers questions about your content An integration with a third-party AI writing tool None of these are agents. They are AI-assisted editing features. Useful, but categorically different from an agent that can receive a natural-language instruction, reason about your content model, take a series of actions, and complete a multi-step content task autonomously. The test Builder.io correctly identifies: can the agent act on the actual asset, through real permissions, leaving a trail the team can inspect? Very few CMS platforms pass that test. Cosmic does. What Cosmic AI Agents actually do Cosmic ships AI Agents that operate directly in your bucket via Slack, WhatsApp, and Telegram. They are not a chat window beside your CMS. They are agents that have authenticated access to your content via the Cosmic API, reason about your object types and schema, and take real actions. Here is what a Cosmic AI Agent can actually do in a single instruction: Read your existing content objects and understand their structure Create, update, or delete objects using your real content model Schedule content for future publishing Search across your bucket using semantic search Generate images via the built-in media library Route drafts for human review before publishing Trigger multi-step Workflows across agents This is not an aspirational roadmap. These are the current, shipped capabilities available today on the Free plan and above. The agent writes to your real content model, in your real bucket, via the same authenticated API your frontend reads from. The draft sits in your CMS for a human editor to review before it ever goes live. The permissions and safety layer This is the part that most "agent-native" marketing skips over, and it is actually the hard part. An agent that can write to your CMS without boundaries is not a feature. It is a liability. What makes agent-native content infrastructure production-ready is the control layer: Scoped API keys. Cosmic agents operate with read/write keys that can be scoped to specific buckets. An agent cannot touch buckets it has not been authorized for. Draft-by-default. Agents create content as drafts. Nothing publishes without a human approval step unless you explicitly configure it otherwise. Full audit trail. Every object creation, update, and publish action is logged in the CMS with a timestamp and actor record. The team can see exactly what the agent did. Workflow checkpoints. Cosmic Workflows let you chain agent steps with human review gates between them. An agent can draft, another can edit, a human approves, and then it publishes. Role-based access. The same permissions model that governs human editors applies to agents. You define what they can touch. This is the answer to the concern that HN threads on AI agent safety keep surfacing: agents do not need unrestricted access to be useful. They need scoped, auditable access. That is what Cosmic's architecture gives you. The content model advantage One thing that rarely gets discussed in the agent-native conversation: structured content models are a prerequisite for agents to do useful work. An agent working inside a page builder that stores everything as a blob of visual components has no semantic understanding of what it is editing. It can move blocks around or swap copy, but it cannot reason about your content as data. A headless CMS with a well-defined content model gives agents something to work with. They know that a object has a , , , , and . They can populate each field with the right type of content, validate against your schema, and produce objects that are immediately usable by your frontend, your search index, and your other agents. Structured content is the foundation that makes agent-native workflows durable rather than brittle. What to actually look for If you are evaluating whether a CMS is genuinely agent-ready, ask these questions: Can an agent create and update content objects via a real, authenticated API, or only via a visual editor? Does the platform ship agents today, or is it on the roadmap? Are agents scoped by permission, or do they have unrestricted bucket access? Is there an audit trail for every agent action? Can agents trigger multi-step workflows with human approval gates? Does the agent work with your actual content model, or with a generic text/blob interface? Cosmic's answer to all six is yes, today, on every paid plan, with a free tier that includes one agent to start. The practical starting point If you want to see what this looks like in practice, the fastest path is to connect a Cosmic AI Agent to your Slack workspace and give it a task: "Draft a blog post about our latest product update and save it as a draft for review." The agent reads your content model, creates the object, sets the status to draft, and posts the CMS link back to your Slack channel. Your editor reviews it in the Cosmic dashboard, makes edits, and publishes. No copy-paste, no manual field mapping, no context lost between the chat window and the CMS. That is what agent-native content infrastructure looks like when it is working. Get started free or book a demo with Tony to see the agent workflow live.
